messages.subject: Re: Size-bias regression in R
parts:
Dear list,

Chris and I had a back-and-forth about his issue which seems to caused
by a optimisation issue. Rather than post a large explanation to the
list reagarding Chris' particular issue, I've written a quick
troubleshooting guide for folks who might be having issues with
optimisation in the Distance (and mrds) R packages.

You can find it here:
https://github.com/dill/Distance/wiki/OptimisationIssues

If you have any further suggestions/addenda then please do reply to me
off list and we can discuss them.


best,
--dave




On 01/10/2013 08:56, David Lawrence Miller wrote:
> > Chris,
> >
> > If you can send me your code off-list I can take a look at this, and we
> > can summarize back to the list once we're done.
> >
> > best,
> > --dave
> >
> >
> > On 01/10/2013 08:51, Chris Hill wrote:
>> >> Many thanks for your responses - Dave, Len & Matthew - very helpful
>> >> indeed.
>> >>
>> >> I have done as suggested and used cluster size as a covariate with
>> >> moderate success:
>> >>
>> >> * Using untransformed cluster size works with species that have a
>> >> smaller range of cluster size, but fails where there is a larger range
>> >> (an obscure error message results see below).
>> >>
>> >> * Using the square root of the cluster size as a covariate works with
>> >> all species and seems to produce sensible results (in this particular
>> >> case, dividing the cluster size by the standard deviation of the size
>> >> values as Dave suggested also yields the error below).
>> >>
>> >> My data are fairly simple - four distance bands (or three if I pool
>> >> the first two bands, which I am minded to do) and cluster sizes that
>> >> are heavily skewed towards small values. This prompts the following
>> >> questions:
>> >>
>> >> 1. Is there any reason why using a covariate with such data would be
>> >> invalid?
>> >> 2. Is using the square root of cluster size a reasonable approach?
>> >>
>> >> Thanks
>> >>
>> >> Chris
>> >> --
>> >> Error message:
>> >> Error in ans.ret[meth, ] <- c(ans$par, ans$value, ans$fevals,
>> >> ans$gevals, :
>> >> number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length
>> >>
>> >> ----------------------------------------------------------
>> >>
>> >>
>> >>
>> >> Hi Chris & list,
>> >>
>> >> Len is correct, including size as a covariate is the way we usually deal
>> >> with group size in mrds/Distance and the "old" size bias regression is
>> >> not included in the packages. It is sometimes necessary to "standardise"
>> >> the size covariate first (by dividing through by the standard deviation
>> >> of the size values) to avoid numerical issues.
>> >>
>> >> Hope this helps,
>> >> --dave
>> >>
>> >>
>> >>
>> >> On 30/09/2013 12:06, Len Thomas wrote:
>>> >>> Hi Chris, list,
>>> >>>
>>> >>> I don't think there is anything built in to mrds or Distance that allows
>>> >>> this exactly (the authors of those packages will contradict me if I'm
>>> >>> wrong), but a good (perhaps even better) alternative would be to include
>>> >>> cluster size as a possible covariate in the detection function model.
>>> >>>
>>> >>> One could write code to implement the old-style size bias regression
>>> >>> models -- would also need code to propagate variance appropriately. Let
>>> >>> me know if you want this and we can likely come up with something.
>>> >>>
>>> >>> Cheers - Len
>>> >>>
